macro.regime: AI-credit shock (now spreading) snaps the relief rally inside a Hormuz-driven energy and sticky-inflation stagflation scare
macro.narrative: Sunday 18 Oct run, as of Fri 16 Oct US close (markets closed all weekend, no new session): Thursday's hot-CPI relief rally reversed sharply Friday as CoreWeave's bonds slipped into distress (Oct-2031 yield above 16%, 5-year CDS near a record ~1,195bp implying >60% five-year default odds), hitting AI-adjacent Nasdaq names far harder (-2.15%) than the broad Dow (-0.34%) and sending VIX up 21% to 19.99 with CNN Fear & Greed down to 23 (Extreme Fear). Over the weekend Bloomberg (17 Oct) reported the scare is broadening into real contagion -- Nebius fell ~10% on the week and data-center peers Applied Digital/IREN each fell ~9%, with junk-bond buyers increasingly freezing AI/data-center issuers out of financing altogether, a genuinely new and more structural worry than Friday's single-name CoreWeave story. Separately, Iran's IRGC Navy said two more tankers caught fire after hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday, taking the tally to at least nine vessels attacked since the prior Sunday and corroborating Kpler data showing Hormuz transit volumes collapsing (~20.8M bbl Oct 8 to ~2.9M bbl Oct 11); Russia's FM Lavrov is due in Tehran Mon 19 Oct for de-escalation talks, a modest counter-signal but unconfirmed as of this run. Fed Chair Warsh's Bangkok remarks gave no explicit October signal, calling AI's development path 'very bumpy' while reaffirming a price-stability focus (CME FedWatch ~85-87% hold odds for Oct 27-28, but December hike odds near 75%), while BOE's Bailey said UK second-round inflation looks 'subdued' yet backed markets pricing a quarter-point BOE hike for Nov 5 -- a reminder other DM central banks are still tightening even as the Fed leans toward a hold. Underneath the credit scare, US inflation inputs stayed uniformly hot this week: September CPI, PPI, and retail sales (headline +0.8%, core ex-auto +0.9%) all beat consensus, while Brent closed Friday at $109.86 (intraday high $110, first time since May) even as the IEA's 20M+ barrel SPR release leans against a sustained spike. Gold ($4,181.10) and silver ($57.13) extended their rally on a Treasury-driven safe-haven bid rather than a dovish pivot -- a fragile dynamic tied to credit and geopolitical fear that could partly unwind on a clean hawkish-leaning Oct 28 hold even as the now-broadening AI-credit contagion and continuing Hormuz escalation argue for a slightly more cautious tilt than Saturday's read.
